idiom_name: hand-written for loop: attempt counter, jittered time.Sleep, context deadline
implementation_notes: Go's standard realisation is a small explicit loop - call, classify, compute the next interval, wait, repeat - because the standard library has no retry primitive and the language's error culture keeps such helpers local; time.Sleep plus a math/rand jitter draw and a context deadline is a handful of lines. When the schedule has to be shared across call sites or configured per dependency, github.com/cenkalti/backoff/v4 is the de-facto library and uses exactly this pattern's parameters (InitialInterval, RandomizationFactor, Multiplier, MaxInterval, MaxElapsedTime) with the documented detail that MaxInterval caps the retry interval while the randomized interval may exceed it. Replace time.Sleep with a select on ctx.Done() whenever the caller's deadline or shutdown must interrupt the wait, and use a concurrency-safe randomness source.
pitfalls: time.Sleep cannot be interrupted, so a shutdown or caller deadline waits out the delay; select on ctx.Done() and reuse a timer you can stop.

A single *math/rand.Rand is not safe for concurrent use, and seeding a fresh generator from the clock inside the call re-synchronizes goroutines; prefer one generator per goroutine or a concurrency-safe source.
cenkalti's ExponentialBackOff is documented as not thread-safe and must be Reset before use, and its MaxInterval caps the pre-jitter interval only.
